b1-v-verhaften: The police find the man who stole the bike and take him to the station. He cannot go home.
A detective puts handcuffs on a thief and tells him he must come along.
The news says the police caught a bank robber yesterday and took him into custody.
b1-n-aufforderung: You get a letter from the tax office telling you to send your documents by Friday.
A neighbor sends a formal message asking you to stop the noise at night.
At a dance a man holds out his hand and asks you to dance with him.
b1-n-distanz: A sign in the queue says to keep two metres of space between you and the others.
The way from your home to the office is 15 km. What is the space between two places called?
You keep some emotional space from your noisy neighbor because you do not want to be close to him.
b1-n-anspruch: After one year of work you have the right to 25 days of paid holiday.
After losing your job the law says you may get money from the state.
A customer says he has a legal right to get his money back, and the shop must pay.
b1-v-gucken: Your friend says: 'Hey, look at that bird on the roof!'
Your little brother opens the door a tiny bit to secretly see what is inside.
Tonight you are going to see a film at home on the sofa. Which informal verb is this?
b1-adj-beruflich: You travel to Hamburg not for a holiday but for your job.
A school helps students choose training for their future working life.
You say you are very happy with your career, but not so happy at home. Which adjective is about your work?
b1-adv-weshalb: Your friend did not come to the party, and you ask for the reason. Which question word do you use?
The shop is closed today, and you wonder for what reason.
A child keeps asking his father about the reason for the rain. Which question word means 'why'?
b1-n-schulden: You borrowed 5000 euros from the bank and have not paid it back. You owe a lot.
Your friend spent too much with credit cards and now owes money to many people.
The company must pay back what it owes, and the amounts are huge. Which plural noun means 'debts'?
b1-n-stecker: The lamp does not work because the end of its cable is not in the wall socket.
You travel to England and need an adapter for the end of your charger cable.
You pull the metal-pronged end of the cable out of the wall.
b1-v-klaeren: You and your colleague had a misunderstanding, so you talk until everything is clear.
Before the trip the team must settle who pays for what.
The two neighbors meet to find a solution to the problem about the fence.
b1-n-gymnastik: In the morning your grandma does stretching exercises for ten minutes in front of an open window.
At school the girls practice rolls and jumps on a mat and a balance beam.
In the sports hall a group of older people does easy exercises to music.
b1-n-herkunft: On the form you must write which country and family you come from.
The label on the honey says the place where it was produced.
A museum label tells where the old vase came from. Which noun means 'origin'?
b1-adj-ernst: Your boss has a stern face and says he must talk about something important. There are no jokes.
The doctor says the illness is not a small cold and could be dangerous.
The teacher says: 'This is not a game and it is not funny.'
b1-n-hinweis: A witness gives the detective a small clue that helps solve the case.
A sign says: 'Please note: the machine takes only coins.'
Your friend gives you a small tip about where to find cheap tickets.
b1-v-verteilen: The teacher gives one sheet to each student in the class.
You spread butter evenly over the whole slice of bread.
Volunteers hand out food packets to people at the market.
b1-n-buerste: You clean the dirty pot with a tool that has stiff hairs.
In the morning you comb your long hair with a tool that has many bristles.
Before polishing your shoes you remove the dust with this tool.
b1-n-experte: Your computer has a strange problem, so a man who knows everything about computers comes to fix it.
On TV a man who has studied the climate for decades explains it to the audience.
In court a man with special knowledge is asked for his professional opinion.
b1-v-hageln: Small balls of ice fall from the sky and hit the car roof loudly.
The weather report says that in the afternoon ice stones will fall from the clouds.
Farmers worry about their fruit trees when ice balls fall from storm clouds.
b1-n-pflaume: At the market you buy small purple fruits with a stone inside.
In autumn your grandmother bakes a cake with halves of a purple fruit on top.
You eat a sweet, dark purple fruit and spit out the hard seed.
b1-adj-abhaengig: A teenager still lives at home and gets money from his parents, so he cannot support himself.
He cannot go a single day without cigarettes. His body needs them.
Your trip is not sure yet, because whether it happens is decided by the weather.
b1-n-virus: The doctor says your flu comes from a tiny germ, not from bacteria, so antibiotics will not help.
A harmful program spreads on your computer and damages your files.
Which tiny thing causes many illnesses, like colds?
b1-v-analysieren: A scientist looks at blood samples carefully to find out what they contain.
In class you study a poem line by line to understand its parts.
The company's expert studies the sales numbers in detail.
b1-n-dauer: The film is two hours long. What word means how long it lasts?
The doctor says the treatment will last six weeks.
On the ticket you see how long the flight takes.
b1-adv-zumindest: You did not win the match, but you scored one goal. You did that, at the very least.
The room is small, but it is clean, at the minimum.
You cannot promise to come, but you say you will phone, as a minimum. Which adverb means 'at least'?
b1-n-einzahlung: At the bank you put 200 euros of cash into your account.
The gym asks for a first payment of 50 euros into its account.
The bank form has a slip for paying money into an account.
b1-adj-pauschal: The hotel offers one price that includes meals, drinks and spa all in one.
Someone says 'all people from that country are the same', a broad statement that ignores differences.
The plumber charges a fixed price of 100 euros, no matter how long the job takes.
b1-n-notfall: A man collapses on the street, and someone shouts for help because it is urgent and dangerous.
On the phone number 112 the operator asks: 'What is the situation?'
A sign says: 'In case of urgent danger, break the glass.'
b1-v-fliessen: A river moves slowly through the valley toward the sea.
You open the tap and water comes out in a stream.
Traffic moves smoothly on the motorway without jams, and cars keep moving.
b1-n-amt: You go to the town building to register your new address.
The new mayor takes up his post.
At the local government building you go to the department for ID cards.
b1-n-gang: In the supermarket you walk down the lane between the shelves to find the milk.
In the car you move the stick to change the speed setting.
The hotel room is down the narrow passage, third door on the left.
b1-v-ausschliessen: The police say they can say with certainty it was not an accident. They have ruled it out.
Because of his bad behavior the club does not allow him to take part anymore and keeps him out.
The doctor says it is not serious, and that a broken bone can be ruled out.
b1-n-untersuchung: The doctor checks your throat, heart and blood pressure at a check-up.
The police look into the causes of the accident over several weeks.
Scientists carry out a study about why the bees are disappearing.
b1-adj-peinlich: You fall off your chair in front of the whole class and your face turns red.
You say hello to a stranger because you think he is your friend, and it is awkward.
You forget your boss's name at the party and feel a bit of shame.
b1-n-krankenwagen: A loud siren sounds, and a white vehicle with a blue light rushes an injured person to hospital.
After the accident the vehicle with paramedics arrived within minutes.
When someone collapses, you dial 112 and ask for this vehicle.
b1-n-spur: In the snow you see small marks left by an animal's feet.
On the motorway there are three marked strips for cars next to each other, and you change to the left one.
The police found a small sign left by the thief: a fingerprint.
b1-v-stuerzen: An old man slips on the ice and falls hard.
A hiker slips on a steep path and falls downhill.
The storm is so strong that a big tree topples over.
b1-n-brieftraeger: Every morning a man in a yellow uniform puts letters in your mailbox.
A dog barks at the man who brings the post.
You wait for a parcel and ask the man who delivers the mail if he has it.
b1-adj-unentschieden: The football match ends one all, and nobody wins.
You cannot choose between two jackets, because you have not made up your mind.
The chess game ends without a winner.
b1-n-versichertenkarte: At the doctor's reception you hand over a plastic card so they know your insurance.
At the pharmacy you show a plastic card from your health insurance company.
You forgot your wallet, and without the card from your insurer the doctor cannot treat you for free.
b1-adv-hierher: You call your friend on the phone and ask him to come to this place. Which adverb means 'to here'?
A child is far away, and you wave and say: 'Come toward me!' Which adverb means 'to here'?
The boss asks how you got to this place.
b1-v-siezen: At work you speak to an older customer with the polite form of 'you', not his first name.
A foreign student asks how to speak politely to strangers. Which verb means to use the formal 'you' with someone?
The new teacher says: 'You may call me by my first name, so we do not have to be formal.'
b1-n-arbeiter: A man in a helmet works at the building site laying bricks.
At the factory a man puts parts on the conveyor belt.
The union represents the men who do physical work.
b1-n-mut: The boy jumps from the high diving board, even though he is afraid.
A firefighter goes into a burning house to help someone, without fear.
It took a lot of bravery to tell your boss you were leaving.
b1-v-geniessen: On holiday you lie in the sun, drink coffee and happily take in every moment.
You slowly eat a piece of chocolate and savor every bite.
You listen to music, close your eyes and feel good.
b1-n-einbahnstrasse: A sign with a white arrow says cars may only drive in one direction on this narrow street.
You drive the wrong way into a street where traffic is only allowed in one direction.
Your navigation says you may not go against the traffic in this kind of street.
b1-adj-speziell: You ask the waiter if they have a particular kind of tea for stomach problems.
The gift is for one specific person, not general.
This tool is made for one job only.
b1-n-hoerer: A man calls the radio show to ask a question. He is one of the people who tune in.
On an old telephone you pick up the part you hold to your ear.
A man who tunes in to the radio show every day writes to the presenter.
b1-n-sucht: He cannot stop gambling even though he has lost his savings. It controls him.
The doctor says smoking can lead to a strong dependence that the body cannot stop.
A clinic helps people who cannot stop drinking. Which noun means 'addiction'?
b1-v-blitzen: During the storm a bright light flashes across the sky.
The new car's metal body sparkles in the sun.
The speed camera lights up in the dark when a car goes too fast.
b1-n-laenge: You measure a table from one end to the other and get 2 metres.
The tailor asks how long the trousers should be.
On the map Berlin lies at 13 degrees east. Which noun means this east-west position?
b1-n-erhoehung: The landlord sends a letter saying the rent will be higher next month.
Your boss gives you more salary after one year.
The government raises the price of fuel. Which noun means 'increase'?
b1-adj-obere: The book is on the highest shelf, and you stretch up to reach it.
In the bunk bed your brother sleeps in the top bed.
At the dentist you open your mouth and he looks at the teeth at the top.
b1-v-abnehmen: You want to be lighter, so you eat less and exercise to lose kilos.
After a full moon, the moon looks smaller each night.
You take the picture down from the wall.
b1-n-finger: You have five of them on each hand, and you point with one of them.
A ring is worn on this body part.
You press the button of the lift with this part of your hand.
b1-n-gewalt: The school has a project against hitting and hurting among pupils.
The storm hit the village with great force and the waves smashed the boats.
The captain has full control over the ship.
b1-adv-jedoch: You like the flat, but it is too expensive. Which word introduces the 'but' part?
The weather forecast says sunshine; however, it rains. Which word means 'however'?
You say: 'I wanted to come; however, I was ill.'
b1-n-gedanke: You are lying in bed and a worry comes into your mind about what you will do tomorrow.
A philosopher writes down an idea about life.
You say sorry because you were lost in what was going on in your mind.
b1-v-abhaengen: You ask if you can come tomorrow, and your friend says it all depends on the weather.
Teenagers spend a lazy afternoon in the park without any plan.
You take the curtains down from the window to wash them.
b1-adj-geheim: You tell your friend something and ask him not to tell anyone.
The code for the safe is only known by you.
A surprise party is planned without the birthday child knowing.
b1-n-zins: The bank pays you a small extra amount each year for keeping your savings there.
Your loan costs extra money every month on top of what you borrowed.
Which noun means the percentage the bank adds to or charges on your money?
b1-n-beleg: After buying shoes the shop gives you a small paper to prove you paid.
The tax office wants proof of your costs, so you send a paper.
An example in a text shows that a claim is true.
b1-v-erkennen: You see your old school friend after 20 years and know it is her immediately.
The doctor sees on the X-ray that there is a crack in your bone.
You see from his face that he is sad.
b1-n-bedienungsanleitung: You bought a new coffee machine and cannot start it. You look for the booklet that explains how to use it.
The washing machine shows an error, so you read the book to find out what the signal means.
The little booklet in the box explains each button of the device.
b1-n-zeitpunkt: You say: 'This is not the right moment to talk about money.'
The doctor asks the exact time when the pain started.
In the new film the moment when the hero arrives is perfect.
b1-adj-staendig: Your neighbor plays loud music all the time, again and again, without stopping.
Your phone keeps ringing and ringing and never stops.
Your boss is always changing his mind, over and over.
b1-v-donnern: In the storm there is a loud rumble in the sky after the flash.
The child hides under the blanket when a big noise comes from the sky.
The weather report says lightning and loud booms are coming.
b1-n-original: You buy a copy of a painting, while the real one by the artist hangs in the museum.
Your friend is a very odd person with a strange, funny way of doing things.
The teacher says: 'Please show the real document, not the photocopy.'
b1-n-hoehe: The plane flies at 10,000 metres above the sea.
The carpenter asks how tall the shelf should be.
b1-n-decke: It is cold at night, so you pull a warm cover over you in bed.
You paint the white surface of the room above your head.
On a picnic you spread a cloth on the grass to sit on.
b1-v-versichern: You pay a company each month so that it pays for the damage if your car is stolen.
Your friend says seriously: 'I promise I will be there on time!'
The manager tells the customers there is no problem and calms them down.
b1-n-essig: You pour a sour liquid and oil on your salad.
For cleaning the kettle you use a sour liquid.
Pickled cucumbers are kept in water, salt and this sour liquid.
b1-adj-verpflichtet: The contract says you must work for the company for at least two years.
Every driver is required by law to wear a seat belt.
Because of the big favor, you feel you owe him something.
b1-adv-ziemlich: The soup is hot, more than a little. You say it is ___ hot.
It is not very cold, but it is quite cold. Which adverb fits between 'a little' and 'very'?
You say the film was good, but not perfect. Which adverb means 'pretty'?
b1-n-abfall: You put the empty bottles, paper and food leftovers in the bin outside.
Sales dropped sharply in the second half of the year.
On the street there is rubbish that people threw away.
b1-v-akzeptieren: Your boss offers a new salary and you say yes.
Your friend does not agree, but he takes your decision.
b1-n-stimmung: After the good news everyone in the office is happy.
At the party the music is great and everyone is dancing. How would you describe the feeling in the room?
You get up grumpy today. How you feel is called what?
b1-n-imbiss: You are a bit hungry at 4 pm and eat something small between meals.
At the train station you buy a sausage at a small stand.
You have a quick, small bite at midday.
b1-adj-neugierig: The child wants to know what is inside the box and keeps asking.
Your neighbor looks through the window to see who is visiting.
You want to know everything about the new colleague.
b1-n-hersteller: The phone is broken, so you contact the company that made it.
On the box it says it was made by a company in Germany.
A car company that builds vehicles is called what?
b1-v-ueberholen: On the motorway a fast car goes past a slow truck.
On the bike path a cyclist rides past a slower one.
The runner moves ahead of the others in the last 100 metres.
b1-n-zusammenarbeit: Two companies work together on a project.
The teacher thanks the class for working together well.
Police and firefighters work together after the accident.
b1-n-behoerde: You need to apply for a visa at an official government office.
An official office of the city sends you a letter.
Which noun means a public office of the government?
b1-v-abheben: The plane leaves the ground and rises into the air.
You take 100 euros out of your bank account at the cash machine.
The phone rings, so you lift the receiver and answer it.
b1-n-anwalt: You have a problem with your landlord, so you hire a man who knows the law to represent you.
In court a man in a black robe speaks for the accused.
Your uncle studied law and gives legal advice.
b1-adj-gemeinsam: You and your friend both like football. You have this in common.
The family takes a holiday together.
A flat has a kitchen that everyone uses.
b1-n-mahlzeit: Breakfast, lunch and dinner are each one of these.
The doctor says you should eat three times a day at regular times.
On the plane they serve food, and it is included in the ticket.
b1-v-schwitzen: In a hot sauna water comes out of your skin.
After running 10 km your shirt is wet.
Before an exam your hands are damp.
b1-n-temperatur: The weather report says it will be 25 degrees.
The nurse puts a thermometer under your arm to check your fever.
You set the oven to 180 degrees.
b1-adv-daher: It is raining, and as a result we stay at home. Which adverb means 'that is why'?
You studied hard, and so you passed. Which word connects the two parts?
You point to a house and say the noise comes from there.
b1-n-garantie: You buy a washing machine, and the shop says that if it breaks within two years they will repair it for free.
On the receipt it says: 'Two years of protection from defects.'
No one can say for sure that it will work. The shop gives you a written promise.
b1-adj-lecker: You taste the pizza and it is wonderful.
Mother's cake tastes so good that you have a second piece.
Which adjective describes food that tastes very good?
b1-n-verbindung: Your internet is down, and the line to the web does not work.
You search for a train route from Munich to Hamburg with changes.
The telephone line is bad, and you cannot hear the other person.
b1-v-sich-irren: You said the shop opens at nine, but it opens at ten. You made a mistake.
You say sorry because you thought a stranger was your friend, but you were wrong.
The teacher says: 'If you think the answer is 5, you are mistaken.'
b1-n-taetigkeit: On the form you are asked what kind of work you do.
Gardening is a relaxing thing to do in your free time.
His job at the hospital includes many different tasks.
b1-n-schriftsteller: A man who writes novels is famous in his country and reads from his new book.
Goethe is a famous German man who wrote plays and poems.
At the book fair you meet the man who wrote your favorite novel.
b1-v-begleiten: Your friend walks with you to the station so you are not alone.
A guide goes along with the tourists in the old town.
The pianist plays along while the singer sings.
b1-n-stil: You like her way of dressing, always elegant and modern.
Your way of writing is very personal.
The architect builds in a modern, simple manner.
b1-adj-riesig: You see an elephant that is much bigger than you thought.
The shopping mall is so large that you get lost.
The portion of ice cream is far bigger than you can eat.
b1-n-ingenieur: A man designs bridges and calculates how much weight they can hold.
At a car company a man develops engines.
Your uncle studied technical subjects at university and works on machines.
b1-n-plastik: Bottles and bags made of this light material are bad for the sea.
Children's toys are often colored, light, and made of this artificial material.
You must not put this kind of container in the microwave.
